title: At some gyms, the New Year’s set keeps memberships longest

facts.fact: Planet Fitness had the bulkiest New Year's spike last year, with 79 percent more new customers signing up in January than in the average month (vendor data).
facts.as_of: last year, per a January 2018 publication
facts.quote: One of the least-expensive options, Planet Fitness, had the bulkiest New Year’s spike last year—79 percent more new customers signed up in January than in the average month.

facts.fact: At Planet Fitness, 66 percent of the January 2017 new-member cohort was still active at 10 months, per the latest vendor data.
facts.quote: the latest data shows that 66 percent of the January 2017 cohort is still active—or at least their autopay accounts are.

facts.fact: Average 10-month retention for the preceding 11 Planet Fitness cohorts was 59 percent, per the vendor's data.
facts.quote: Average 10-month retention for the preceding 11 cohorts was only 59 percent.

facts.fact: Planet Fitness offers a monthly membership fee of $10.
facts.quote: Planet Fitness offers a monthly fee of only $10 and advertises a “judgement-free” environment

facts.fact: New Equinox customers can expect a monthly fee in excess of $150.
facts.quote: new Equinox customers can expect a monthly fee in excess of $150.

facts.fact: Equinox customers spend an average of $323 in their first month, per vendor data.
facts.quote: lead Equinox customers to spend an average of $323 in their first month—and spending balloons from there.

facts.fact: Equinox customers spend on average $1,520 in the first year of membership, more than triple what customers spend at other gyms, per vendor data.
facts.quote: Equinox customers spend, on average, $1,520 in the first year of membership—more than triple what customers spend at other gyms.

facts.fact: Pure Barre saw as much as 53 percent more new customers than average in last January, per vendor data.
facts.as_of: last January, per a January 2018 publication
facts.quote: They too see a swell of new customers—as much as 53 percent more than average at Pure Barre last January.

facts.fact: A single boutique studio class ranges from $20 to more than $30.
facts.quote: With a single class ranging from $20 to more than $30, boutique fitness can make Equinox look like a bargain.

facts.fact: At SoulCycle, Pure Barre, and YogaWorks, new customers spend less than $300 in their first year on average, per vendor data.
facts.quote: At SoulCycle, Pure Barre, and YogaWorks, new customers spend less than $300 in their first year, on average.

facts.fact: At the end of their first year, more than 80 percent of boutique studio customers do not spend in the last quarter, with one exception, per vendor data.
facts.quote: at the end of their first year, more than 80 percent of boutique customers don’t spend in the last quarter—with one exception.

facts.fact: Quarterly retention at ClassPass averaged 39 percent at the end of the year, versus 16 percent for other boutique brands, per vendor data.
facts.quote: Quarterly retention at ClassPass averaged 39 percent at the end of year, whereas retention at the other boutique-brands averaged just 16 percent.

facts.fact: Bloomberg Second Measure launched a new exclusive transaction dataset in July 2022, and the vendor advises against using historical posts to infer period-over-period comparisons.
facts.quote: do not_**_support referring to historical blog posts to infer period-over-period comparisons.
